answers.value: All risks bound in the period that carry a ceded reinsurance placement (facultative certificates and treaty cessions) requiring a cession advice to Reinsurance Accounting for bordereau and treaty reporting; scope = one bind batch keyed to the policy/certificate number in Guidewire PolicyCenter.

The current bordereau reporting cycle — cessions with an effective/bind date in the reporting month (e.g. 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30); advices are sent within 2 business days of bind so accounting can meet the monthly bordereau close.

Each cession advice carries: policy/certificate number, cedent and reinsurer, treaty/fac reference, ceded percentage and limit, ceded premium and brokerage, effective date, and layer. Any advice missing reinsurer, ceded premium, or treaty reference is returned to the underwriter before send.

Count and ceded-premium total of advices sent reconciles to the ceded entries posted in Sapiens ReinsurancePro for the batch; ceded premium on the advice must equal the ceded amount on the bound risk to the cent (delta = 0).
Sent advice (email + Sapiens transaction) retained under /Reinsurance/Cessions/<policy-number>/ with send timestamp and version; retained 7 years per treaty record-keeping policy.

Cessions that fail to notify (bounced advice, missing treaty mapping) are logged as an exception in the ceded queue with disposition (remap treaty / correct data / re-send), owner = Reinsurance Accountant, cleared within 2 business days.

Sampled advices trace back to the ceded reinsurance screen on the bound risk in PolicyCenter and to the treaty slip; ceded percentage on the advice matches the treaty schedule for that line and layer.
Cession status moves Bound to Ceded-Advised only after the advice is confirmed sent; no risk sits in Ceded-Pending beyond the 2-business-day SLA.
Cession effective date equals the policy bind/effective date; advice send date is on or before the bordereau cut-off; dates align to the treaty reporting calendar.
All ceded risks bound in the reporting month (census); each advice checked for completeness and for a matching ceded entry in Sapiens ReinsurancePro.

PASS = 100% of ceded binds have an advice sent within 2 business days with ceded premium matching the posted entry. FAIL = any ceded bind without an advice, or advice ceded premium differing from the posted ceded entry.
Late or failed advices are escalated to Reinsurance Accounting and the Reinsurance Ops Manager; the cession is held out of the bordereau until corrected and re-advised.

Delegation matrix in the reinsurance procedures manual sets who may advise/confirm cessions by treaty and ceded-limit band; only Underwriters and Underwriting Assistants under an active treaty mandate can release advices, per authority matrix v3.2.

Acceptance criteria: cession advice sent within 2 business days of bind, all mandatory fields present, ceded premium equal to posted ceded entry, and receipt acknowledged by Reinsurance Accounting. Evidence: sent advice + Sapiens transaction ID, filed under /Reinsurance/Cessions/<policy-number>/ and linked on the bound-risk record.

answers.value: The newly bound/issued policy whose renewal diary must be seeded; scope = one policy record in Guidewire PolicyCenter for which an expiry-driven renewal review date is being set.

Every in-force policy has exactly one active renewal diary entry; count of bound policies without a diary date must be 0 on the daily book-in-force reconciliation.
Diary entry and the system-calculated dates are stored on the policy record in PolicyCenter with a set timestamp and the calculating user; change history retained for the policy life plus 3 years.

Policies where the diary cannot be auto-set (missing expiry, non-standard term) are logged to the renewals exception queue with disposition (correct term / manual diary), owner = Renewal Underwriter, cleared within 2 business days.
Sampled diary entries trace to the policy expiry field on the declarations page; the -90d/-60d offsets recompute correctly from that expiry date.
Policy status is Issued/In-Force before a renewal diary is set; diary status flips to Active and later to Worked as the renewal cycle progresses.
Renewal-review date, broker-quote date and non-renewal-notice date all derive from expiry and satisfy the earliest state statutory notice window (longest lead state governs).
Pre/post: before, the policy has no diary and would age past its renewal window; after, the diary shows review at expiry -90d; comparison logged against the issuance change record.
Diary set is linked to the policy issuance work item / bind transaction number in PolicyCenter; no separate change ticket is raised for the standard diary set.
All policies issued in the day's bind batch (census); each checked for a single active renewal diary with correct offset dates.
PASS = 100% of issued policies have a renewal diary at expiry -90d with an assigned renewal underwriter. FAIL = any in-force policy with no diary or a review date inside the statutory notice window.
Missing or mis-dated diaries are corrected same day and re-verified; recurring gaps for a product are raised to UW Operations to fix the diary-calculation rule.
Acceptance = one active diary per in-force policy, review date = expiry -90d, non-renewal trigger set to the governing state window, assignee populated.
Evidence = diary record and change history on the policy in PolicyCenter, plus the daily book-in-force diary-coverage report retained under /Renewals/Diary-Coverage/.

In-scope effective dates: diary set at issuance, effective for the policy term; renewal-review date = expiry -90d and non-renewal-notice date set to the earliest applicable state statutory window for the term ending on policy expiry.

answers.value: The final issued policy documents for a bound risk — declarations, schedule, forms, endorsements and disclosures — to be archived with a retention period set; scope = one issued policy package moved to the OpenText document repository.

Document count archived equals the count in the issued package (declarations + schedule + each form/endorsement + disclosures); index count in OpenText reconciles to the PolicyCenter document list (delta = 0).

Records-retention schedule v2.3 (approved by the Records Manager and Compliance) governs retention classes and disposition rules applied at archive.
Sensitivity: retention class is driven by document type and jurisdiction; a change in governing state can extend the retention period, which the schedule re-evaluates at archive.
Materiality: any missing statutory document (e.g. a required disclosure) is a material archive defect and blocks completion; cosmetic metadata gaps are logged but non-blocking.
Sampled archived documents trace to the issued versions in PolicyCenter; the archived PDF matches the delivered policy document byte-for-byte (same version hash).
Policy status is Issued before documents are archived; document status moves to Archived with retention applied.
Issue date, archive date and computed disposition date are consistent; disposition date = issue date + retention period for the class.
All policies issued in the period plus a monthly 5% back-sample of prior archives (census of new issues; sample of history).
PASS = 100% of issued packages fully archived with correct retention class and no missing statutory documents. FAIL = any issued policy with an incomplete archive or unset retention.
Incomplete archives are re-ingested and re-verified; recurring gaps for a document type are raised to Records Management to fix the ingestion mapping.
Retention effective from the policy issue date; the archived version is the final issued version effective on that date.

Sensitivity: the acknowledgement requirement and acceptable proof vary by state and coverage; a state change re-evaluates whether a signed acknowledgement is mandatory.
Materiality: a missing statutory acknowledgement (e.g. UM/UIM rejection) is material and must be obtained; a discretionary read-receipt gap is low-materiality but still tracked.
Sampled confirmations trace to the delivered document version and to the DocuSign envelope / portal receipt for that policy; signer matches the named insured or authorized representative.
Policy delivery status advances to Acknowledged only when a valid signed acknowledgement or receipt is on file; otherwise it stays Awaiting-Acknowledgement.
Acknowledgement timestamp is on or after the delivery date and within the statutory window for the policy effective date.
All policies requiring acknowledgement in the period (census); each checked for a valid captured signed acknowledgement or receipt.

PASS = 100% of acknowledgement-required policies have a valid signed acknowledgement/receipt on file within the statutory window. FAIL = any required policy without a captured acknowledgement past the window.
Outstanding acknowledgements are resent and chased; if still not returned, an alternate proof of delivery is obtained and the case escalated to the Underwriter/Compliance.
Acknowledgement requirement effective as of the policy effective date; the state-rule version in force on that date determines whether a signed acknowledgement is mandatory.

Applicable rule/citation: state proof-of-delivery and signed-acknowledgement statutes/regulations for the risk state (e.g. UM/UIM selection-rejection acknowledgement, coverage-rejection acknowledgement forms); the governing citation and required proof type are recorded against the policy in the compliance evidence record.

checklist.step: File the delivery acknowledgement
checklist.value: The signed acknowledgement or delivery receipt is filed on the policy so proof of delivery is evidenced.

testing.value: Sampled acknowledgement-required policies each carry a captured acknowledgement; 0 required policies without proof of delivery.

checklist.step: Maintain an acknowledgement audit trail
checklist.value: Envelope/receipt IDs, signer identity and timestamps are captured and non-editable, linked to the delivered document version.

testing.value: For 25 sampled policies per quarter the acknowledgement traces to the delivered document and signer; 0 untraceable acknowledgements.

answers.value: The full policy package for a bound risk being assembled for the insured and producing broker — declarations, schedule, forms/endorsements, disclosures and invoice — ready to dispatch; scope = one policy's package prepared in Guidewire PolicyCenter.
Prepared at issuance for the current policy term, immediately after schedule assembly and disclosure confirmation, within the 1-business-day post-issue preparation SLA.

Package must contain: declarations page, full schedule, all forms/endorsements, all mandatory disclosures, and the billing/invoice insert, addressed to the correct broker and insured. Preparation is blocked if any component is missing or the recipient details are incomplete.
Package component count = the components required by the issuance checklist for the product/state (delta = 0); the assembled package version matches the confirmed schedule and disclosure set.

Prepared package (single rendered PDF set) saved on the policy in PolicyCenter and copied to OpenText under /Policies/<policy-number>/issued/ with version and timestamp; retained per the records schedule.

Packages missing a component (form, disclosure, invoice) are held in the preparation exception queue with disposition (add component / re-render), owner = Underwriting Assistant, cleared before dispatch.
Policy package/issuance checklist v4.1 (approved by UW Operations) defines the required package components by product and state.
Sensitivity: the required component set varies by product and state; a state or coverage change re-runs the issuance checklist and may add forms/disclosures before the package is complete.
Materiality: a missing statutory disclosure or the wrong schedule version is material and blocks dispatch; a cover-letter formatting issue is non-blocking.
Sampled prepared packages trace to the confirmed schedule and disclosure set in PolicyCenter; the package version equals the assembled/confirmed versions.
Package status is Ready-to-Deliver only after schedule assembly and disclosure confirmation are complete; otherwise it stays In-Preparation.
Package preparation date is on or after issuance and before dispatch; effective/expiry dates on the declarations match the bound policy.
All policies issued in the day's batch (census); each package checked for a complete component set matching the issuance checklist.

PASS = 100% of packages contain every required component (declarations, schedule, forms, disclosures, invoice) for the correct recipients. FAIL = any package missing a required component or with wrong recipient details.
Incomplete packages are re-rendered with the missing component and re-verified before dispatch; recurring gaps for a product are raised to UW Operations to fix the checklist/template.
Source-system fields: PolicyCenter policy_number, package_component_type, version, recipient_broker, insured_contact, effective_date.
Control total: assembled package component count equals the issuance-checklist required-component count for the product/state (delta = 0).

checklist.step: Include current filed forms and disclosures in the package
checklist.value: All forms and mandatory disclosures added to the package are the current filed editions for the risk state.

testing.value: Sampled packages use current filed forms/disclosures; 0 packages prepared with a superseded or missing statutory component.

checklist.step: Document the prepared package on the file
checklist.value: The final package version and component list are recorded on the policy so the prepared package is evidenced.

testing.value: Sampled files contain the complete prepared package; 0 packages dispatched without a documented component set.

checklist.step: Version the prepared package with an audit trail
checklist.value: Package preparation and re-renders are timestamped and versioned in PolicyCenter/OpenText.

testing.value: For 25 sampled packages per quarter the prepared version reconciles to the assembled schedule and disclosure set; 0 unversioned packages.
